Towards Transparent Multi-Agent Systems.work: A MARL-trained policy for 4-robot warehouse coordination is a 128-neuron network: uninterpretable. Knowledge distillation extracts the learned strategy into a behavior tree with symbolic rules: if (zone-congestion > 0.7) route-to [north-entry]; if (robot-idle-time > 30s) assist-peer; etc. The tree achieves 92% of the RL policy’s reward, and a human operator can now read the 11 rules and understand why the system behaves as it does, enabling safe deployment in safety-critical warehouses.

The move: distill via minBT KL(π || π_BT), teaching the tree to match the learned policy's action distribution. Why it holds: a behavior tree's decisions are human-readable (each node is a condition or action), so minimizing KL divergence makes the tree behavior-equivalent to the opaque policy while remaining transparent.

CATNet: Collaborative Alignment under La.work: Two vehicles detect a pedestrian. Car A uses 64-channel lidar (dense returns), Car B uses 32-channel with 80 ms message delay. Without temporal alignment, Car B's data is from where the pedestrian was 80 ms ago. Applying spatio-temporal sync + wavelet denoising to align their coordinate frames and timestamps: detection confidence improves, overlapping false positives drop. Average Precision climbs from baseline to +5.7 points, or ~68 → 73.7 AP on V2XSet.
CATNet: Collaborative Alignment under La.math: The object is the fused estimate x̂ of a shared environment state given asynchronous sensor reports zi(ti) from agent i at reception time t. The move: resynchronize each delayed report via temporal interpolation and apply wavelet denoising to reduce noise variance zi′ = Denoise(Interp(zi, t − ti)), then weight the aligned observations by sensor reliability in the fused posterior. Why it holds: aligning time and geometry before fusion ensures that each robot's belief is conditioned on the true state at the fusion instant, removing the bias introduced by fusing reports from different temporal snapshots.
